Bug_Title: SA: Nonsensical self computation involving a field (e.g., x & x) (SA_FIELD_SELF_COMPUTATION)
Bug_Details:
This method performs a nonsensical computation of a field with another
reference to the same field (e.g., x&x or x-x). Because of the nature
of the computation, this operation doesn't seem to make sense,
and may indicate a typo or a logic error. Double-check the computation.
Bug_Explanation: The code performs a bitwise AND operation on the variable 'x' with itself (x & x), which is nonsensical because the result will always be the same as the original value of 'x'. This operation likely indicates a logic error or a typo in the code.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case 'testShowBug' calls the 'showBug' method from the 'SelfComputationExample' class. This method contains a nonsensical operation where the field 'x' is computed with itself using the bitwise AND operator (x & x). The test asserts that the result should not be 0, but since 'x & x' will always return the value of 'x', which is 42 in this case, the assertion fails, thus triggering the bug.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results indicate that the test passed successfully, as shown by 'OK (1 test)'. This suggests that the assertion 'assertNotEquals(0, result)' did not fail, meaning the result was not 0. Therefore, the test did not confirm the presence of the bug as described.
